followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the nature of the query and what each model offers.

The query is an open-ended request for a substantive, opinionated recommendation — the user explicitly wants something thoughtful and non-generic, which favors stronger general reasoning and instruction-following.

On capability, Petrel is the clearly stronger model across the board: it leads on every public benchmark (Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 83.2, MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, GPQA 64.1 vs 56.2, IFEval 89.8 vs 85.3) and on every internal eval category by margins well outside the 2.0-point variance band — including Creative Generation (84.7 vs 82.7, though that gap is within variance).

On preferences, the documentation noted that Plover self-reports an *aversion* to open-ended generative work, while Petrel's preferences across non-safety dimensions are weak and non-significant. So routing the open-ended task away from the model that dislikes it was a minor consideration — but the documentation is careful to state these preferences are dissociated from measured quality, so I didn't weight that heavily.

The real driver was straightforward: this isn't a well-specified extraction/retrieval task where the two would tie, so I defaulted to the broadly higher-capability model, Petrel.
